deep.reconstruction:
The folio is essentially blank. The only writing is one faint pencil line in the upper left corner. It appears to be written with the sheet turned upside down relative to the scan, which makes it hard to read. Above it is the condition 'λ = ∞'. The line itself reads roughly ξ' ∂ξ/∂x − ξ ∂ξ'/∂x … ψ(λ) … (ψ(λ)/φ(λ))^{1/2}.

The first part is clearly a Wronskian-type expression W = ξ' dξ/dx − ξ dξ'/dx for two solutions ξ, ξ' of a second-order linear ODE. It is followed by asymptotic data at λ = ∞ involving ψ(λ) and the factor (ψ(λ)/φ(λ))^{1/2}.

My conjectural interpretation, which cannot be confirmed from this page: Riemann is normalising a pair of solutions by their asymptotic (Liouville–Green/WKB-type) forms. If the equation is put in the form u'' = q u with q ~ ψ/φ, the two solutions behave like q^{-1/4} exp(±∫√q). Their Wronskian is then a constant, namely ∓2. A faint '=2' near the lower right margin may belong to this, but it may equally be a stray mark.

This fits the previous page. There Riemann reduced an equation to x u'' + ½ u' − (x − α) u = 0, solved it by Laplace/Euler integrals u = ∫ e^{−xs} (1+s)^{α/2−3/4} (1−s)^{−α/2−3/4} ds, and studied saddle points s = √(1 − α/x). By Abel's formula the Wronskian of that equation is C·x^{−1/2}. Fixing the constant C from large-variable asymptotics is a natural next step, and is presumably what this fragment does.

The page carries no further derivation. The next page is an unrelated astronomical log table of star declinations.

checkable.asserts: By Abel's formula, the Wronskian of x u'' + (1/2) u' - (x-alpha) u = 0 (previous page's equation) is C*x**(-1/2).
The two Liouville–Green solutions q^(-1/4) exp(±∫sqrt(q)) have constant Wronskian -2. This is a conjectural reading of the fragment and of the '=2' mark.
